problem: Existing visual semantic (object-goal) navigation models work for a single agent finding a single target; they are inefficient and fragile for multiple targets. Prior multi-agent embodied work (FurnLift/FurnMove) only handles two agents on a single task, not several agents with multiple subtasks under bandwidth limits.
motivation: Searching for several objects in a room with one robot is slow and a single wrong decision can fail the whole task. Multiple agents can share information and split the search, but they need efficient exploration and must communicate under limited bandwidth. Scene priors (object co-occurrence) can further guide search.
key_idea: A hierarchical multi-agent framework in which each agent builds a semantic map, marks target and prior-related key objects, exchanges compressed encoded maps with nearby agents, and uses PPO to choose map sub-goals that a shortest-path planner executes.
insight: The ablations show the semantic map matters most: removing it drops AI2-THOR known-object N=1 SR from 45.19 to 30.33. Scene priors (w/o SP. gives 41.00 SR) and hierarchical sub-goal decisions (w/o HieDec. gives 38.88 SR) each give further gains. Near-Central performance suggests the encoded-map communication with proximity-based agent selection loses little information.
method: Semantic mapping: fine-tuned Mask-RCNN segmentation plus depth and pose are projected into a top-down 2D semantic map (5cm grid) with K+2 channels (object categories, occupied, explored).
Key objects mapping: a scene prior knowledge graph built from Visual Genome marks target objects and related objects on a 2-layer key objects map.

Communication: a pretrained conv encoder/decoder compresses the semantic map into a vector (trained with pixel-wise reconstruction loss); agents only send to other agents within a 1.0 m-extended field-of-view area to save bandwidth.
Feature fusion: a CNN over the concatenated semantic and key-objects maps, plus FC features of pose and last action, form the state feature.
High-level decision: PPO actor-critic outputs a map sub-goal every d=10 steps; reward is 0.7 * decrease in distance to the nearest target + 0.3 * decrease in distance to the nearest key object.
Low-level decision: modified BFS shortest path on the updated semantic map (occupied channel = obstacles) generates the discrete actions toward the sub-goal.

setting.backbone: Mask-RCNN (fine-tuned) + small CNN/FC encoders + PPO actor-critic (trained from scratch) + BFS planner
setting.training_data: AI2-THOR: 80 train scenes, 7900 tasks; RoboTHOR: 60 train scenes, 5940 tasks; Mask-RCNN fine-tuned on simulator RGB/segmentation; encoder/decoder trained on 20 scenes; scene prior graph from Visual Genome
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + pose per agent, plus messages from other agents
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead 0.25 m, Rotate L/R 90°, LookUp/Down 30°, Found, Done (high-level policy outputs map sub-goals)
setting.privileged: none stated (pose given; Mask-RCNN fine-tuned with GT segmentation from simulator during training)

numbers_note: Custom multi-agent benchmark (no canonical benchmark); tables report N=1..5 for known/unknown objects; only representative N entries listed. Test splits are unseen scenes with no official split name.
results: With 5 agents in AI2-THOR (known objects) the method reaches SR 48.02 / SPL 23.30 / EI 43.60, beating the best decentralized baseline Cordial Sync (37.15 / 17.82 / 39.35) and Central w/o SP. (44.50 / 18.39 / 40.36). It is close to the Central upper bound (48.90 SR). Similar gains hold in RoboTHOR and for unknown target objects.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation (AI2-THOR/RoboTHOR) with a custom task and metrics; no real-robot tests
Relies on a fine-tuned Mask-RCNN and pose, and a fixed communication radius rule, not learned communication; absolute SR stays below 50%
builds_on: Visual semantic navigation using scene priors (Yang et al.)
